title: Encoding characterization of undirected path reachability
statement: A binary string $x$ encodes an undirected graph with $n$ vertices and designated vertices $s,t$ that are connected by a path if and only if there exist natural numbers $n,s,t$ and a witness that $x$ has the following format: $n$ copies of the pair $11$, followed by the separator $01$; then $n^2$ adjacency bits, each duplicated as $00$ or $11$, followed by $01$; then the bits of $s$, each duplicated, followed by $01$; and finally the ordinary binary expansion of $t$, occupying the entire remaining suffix. The format requires $s<n$ and $t<n$; the adjacency relation encoded by the matrix must be symmetric, and there must be a path from $s$ to $t$ using edges whose corresponding bits in $x$ are $1$.
hypotheses_covered: There exist natural numbers $n,s,t$ and a witness that $x$ has the specified format
The encoded adjacency relation is symmetric
There is a path from $s$ to $t$ in the encoded graph
